example:
a, b, c = Node("a"), Node("b"), Node("c")
a.next, b.next, c.next = b, c, b
cycle_entry(a)
start: Draw `a → b → c → b` and walk it with your finger. The answer is the first node the walk comes back to: `b`, the node itself, compared with `is`, never by its value.

A set of visited nodes finds it, but the rules ask for constant extra space. Walk two pointers from `head` instead: `slow` one step at a time, `fast` two. If `fast` runs off the end there is no loop. If they land on the same node there is one, but that meeting node is usually not the entry.

start.text: After they meet, put a third pointer at `head` and move it and `slow` one step at a time. They meet at the entry. The shape, with the moves left to you:

test_every_small_prefix_and_cycle_length: Every list up to 24 nodes, with the loop coming back at every position, and every node holding `7`. Anything that compares `.value` sees one node where there are many: compare nodes with `is`.
It also checks that no `next` link changed. Marking nodes as visited by rewriting `next` is not allowed: finding the loop must only read the list.
test_long_chain_and_invalid_links: A 10,000-node list with no loop. A recursive walk hits Python's recursion limit long before the end, so walk it with a loop.
`cycle_entry(42)`, `cycle_entry("node")`, and a node whose `next` is `42` must each raise `ValueError`. Check the type of `head`, and of every node you step onto.

AttributeError: You read `.next` on something that is not a node, usually `None` at the end of the list. Check `fast is not None and fast.next is not None` before moving `fast` two steps.
RecursionError: The tests walk a 10,000-node list, and Python stops recursion at about 1,000 calls. Turn the recursion into a `while` loop.

stopped: A second loop that never ends almost always has one pointer standing still. Both `p` and `slow` have to move one step on every turn, or they never meet. Put a breakpoint inside the loop and watch which one stays put.
If the first loop never ends, `fast` is not moving two steps, or the loop only stops when `fast` is `None`, which never happens in a list with a loop. Stop as soon as `slow is fast`.
passing: All passing. Build a long chain as your own input, say 100,000 nodes with the last one pointing back to the middle, and check the memory: it should not grow with the length. That is the constant space the rules asked for.
